symbols.name: n
symbols.def: Total number of experimental units.

symbols.name: Kf
symbols.def: Number \(K_f\) of binary treatment factors.

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: \(Q=2^{K_f}\), the number of treatment combinations.

symbols.name: F
symbols.def: \(F=Q-1\), the number of nonconstant factorial contrasts.

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: Dimension of the baseline vector.

symbols.name: W
symbols.def: Fixed loss-weight matrix for the factorial vector.

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: Exact target acceptance probability \(\alpha\).

symbols.name: eta
symbols.def: Positive-support mixture weight \(\eta\).

symbols.name: Qset
symbols.def: Treatment-combination set \(\mathcal Q\).

symbols.name: C
symbols.def: Factorial contrast matrix \(\mathbf C\) with the nonconstant Walsh characters as columns and row vectors \(c_q^{\mathsf T}\), \(q\in\mathcal Q\).

symbols.name: Xn
symbols.def: Complete baseline array \(\mathbf X_n=(x_{1n},\ldots,x_{nn})\), observed before assignment.

symbols.name: nu
symbols.def: Limit \(\nu\) of the empirical baseline measures.

symbols.name: Yn
symbols.def: Fixed realized table \(\mathbf Y_n=\{Y_{in}(q):i\le n,q\in\mathcal Q\}\) for design-based analysis.

symbols.name: taun
symbols.def: \(\boldsymbol\tau_n=2^{1-K_f}\mathbf C^{\mathsf T}(n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf Y_{in})\), the realized finite-population factorial vector.

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: Dimension of the oracle quotient coordinate.

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: Dimension of the nuisance coordinate.

symbols.name: rho
symbols.def: Oracle-relevant quotient coordinate \(\rho\).

symbols.name: lambda
symbols.def: Outcome nuisance coordinate \(\lambda\).

symbols.name: beta
symbols.def: Full conditional-outcome parameter \(\beta=(\rho,\lambda)\).

symbols.name: Urho
symbols.def: Oracle-coordinate chart domain \(\mathcal U_{\rho}\).

symbols.name: Ulambda
symbols.def: Nuisance-coordinate chart domain \(\mathcal U_{\lambda}\).

symbols.name: U
symbols.def: Regular identifiable chart \(\mathcal U=\mathcal U_{\rho}\times\mathcal U_{\lambda}\).

symbols.name: Kclass
symbols.def: Global parameter set \(\mathcal K\).

symbols.name: mu
symbols.def: Common dominating measure \(\mu\) for the conditional outcome family.

symbols.name: Pbeta
symbols.def: Stable conditional potential-outcome family dominated by \(\mu\); its draw is used only to average exact design risks.

symbols.name: score
symbols.def: Conditional score \(s_{q,\beta}(Y(q)\mid X)\) of the outcome family.

symbols.name: Info
symbols.def: \(I(\beta)=Q^{-1}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}\int E_{\beta}[s_{q,\beta}s_{q,\beta}^{\mathsf T}\mid x]\,\nu(dx)\).

symbols.name: Ieff
symbols.def: \(I_{\mathrm{eff}}(\beta)=I_{\rho\rho}-I_{\rho\lambda}I_{\lambda\lambda}^{-1}I_{\lambda\rho}\).

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: A wave-specific subset \(T\) of units, with size \(k=|T|\).

symbols.name: Tfull
symbols.def: \(T_n^{\mathrm{full}}=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), the experiment-induced full-array sequence.

symbols.name: tauT
symbols.def: \(\boldsymbol\tau_T=2^{1-K_f}\mathbf C^{\mathsf T}(|T|^{-1}\sum_{i\in T}\mathbf Y_{in})\), the realized factorial vector on \(T\).

symbols.name: OmegaT
symbols.def: Balanced assignment support \(\Omega_T=\{z\in\mathcal Q^{T}:\sum_{i\in T}\mathbf 1\{z_i=q\}=|T|/Q,\ q\in\mathcal Q\}\).

symbols.name: ZT
symbols.def: Wave assignment \(Z_T\).

symbols.name: DeltaT
symbols.def: \(\Delta_T(z)=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}(2^{1-K_f}c_q)\otimes\{|T|/Q\}^{-1}\sum_{i\in T:z_i=q}(x_{in}-\bar x_T)\), the factorial covariate-imbalance vector.

symbols.name: Action
symbols.def: Centered trace-normalized ellipsoidal score matrix \(H\).

symbols.name: aTG
symbols.def: Exact lower-tail acceptance function \(a_{T,H}\) of the scores \(\Delta_T(z)^{\mathsf T}H\Delta_T(z)\), with a common randomized probability on the boundary score and \(|\Omega_T|^{-1}\sum_z a_{T,H}(z)=\alpha\).

symbols.name: piTG
symbols.def: \(\pi_{iq}(T,H)=\sum_{z\in\Omega_T}p_{T,H}(z)\mathbf 1\{z_i=q\}\).

symbols.name: HTTG
symbols.def: \(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(H)=|T|^{-1}\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}2^{1-K_f}c_q\mathbf 1\{Z_i=q\}Y_{in}(q)/\pi_{iq}(T,H)\).

symbols.name: VTG
symbols.def: \(V_T(H,\beta)=E_{\beta}E_{p_{T,H}}[(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(H)-\boldsymbol\tau_T)^{\mathsf T}W(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(H)-\boldsymbol\tau_T)\mid\mathbf X_n]\).

symbols.name: BmapT
symbols.def: \(\mathcal B_T(\beta)=\operatorname{Cov}_{\beta}\{\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(0),\Delta_T\}\operatorname{Var}(\Delta_T)^{+}\), the empirical Gaussian projection of the factorial estimator on imbalance.

symbols.name: Norm
symbols.def: Trace normalization with a zero convention.

symbols.name: GT
symbols.def: \(G_T(\beta)=\mathcal N\{\mathcal B_T(\beta)^{\mathsf T}W\mathcal B_T(\beta)\}\), the empirical Gaussian raw-MSE oracle score.

symbols.name: Ginf
symbols.def: \(G_{\infty}(\beta)\), the common oracle-map limit along the full-array and random-complement sequences, derived by \(\mathrm{lem{:}experiment\text{-}indexed\text{-}oracle\text{-}convergence}\).

symbols.name: Zgauss
symbols.def: \(Z\sim N(0,I_{Fp})\), the standardized Gaussian imbalance.

symbols.name: phiGauss
symbols.def: \(\varphi_{Fp}(z)=(2\pi)^{-Fp/2}\exp(-z^{\mathsf T}z/2)\), the standard Gaussian density.

symbols.name: qGauss
symbols.def: \(q_{\alpha,\beta}=\inf\{u>0:\Pr(Z^{\mathsf T}G_{\infty}(\beta)Z\le u)\ge\alpha\}\), the Gaussian quantile induced by the common experiment-indexed oracle limit.

symbols.name: fGauss
symbols.def: \(f_{\beta}(u)=\frac{d}{du}\Pr\{Z^{\mathsf T}G_{\infty}(\beta)Z\le u\}\) for \(u>0\).

symbols.name: boundaryCov
symbols.def: For \(g_{\beta}(z)=z^{\mathsf T}G_{\infty}(\beta)z\) and \(\psi_{a,\beta}(z)=z^{\mathsf T}D_{\rho_a}G_{\infty}(\beta)z\), \(\mathcal C_{ab}(\beta,u)\) is the continuous coarea version of \(\operatorname{Cov}\{\psi_{a,\beta}(Z),\psi_{b,\beta}(Z)\mid g_{\beta}(Z)=u\}\): each conditional raw moment is the ratio \[\frac{\int_{g_{\beta}^{-1}(u)}h(z)\varphi_{Fp}(z)\lVert\nabla_z g_{\beta}(z)\rVert^{-1}d\mathcal H^{Fp-1}(z)}{\int_{g_{\beta}^{-1}(u)}\varphi_{Fp}(z)\lVert\nabla_z g_{\beta}(z)\rVert^{-1}d\mathcal H^{Fp-1}(z)},\] with \(h=\psi_{a,\beta}\psi_{b,\beta},\psi_{a,\beta},\psi_{b,\beta}\), and covariance is the first ratio minus the product of the latter two ratios; values at removable chart points use the unique continuous extension.

symbols.name: rankG
symbols.def: Common positive rank \(r_G\) of the oracle score on the regular chart.

symbols.name: dT
symbols.def: \(d_T(\beta)=V_T(0,\beta)-V_T(G_T(\beta),\beta)\), the empirical-oracle gain over balanced complete randomization.

symbols.name: Mbal
symbols.def: \(\mathcal M_n=\{m\in\{Q,2Q,\ldots,n-Q\}:Q\mid(n-m)\}\), the admissible balanced pilot sizes for which both waves are balanced.

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: Balanced pilot size \(m\).

symbols.name: N
symbols.def: Main-wave size \(N=n-m\).

symbols.name: Sm
symbols.def: Uniform random pilot subset \(S_m\), drawn before its balanced complete randomization.

symbols.name: Tmain
symbols.def: \(T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}=S_m^c\), the experiment-induced random-complement sequence, with convergence in probability taken over the uniform pilot split.

symbols.name: Opilot
symbols.def: Pilot information \(\mathcal O_m=\sigma(S_m,Z_{S_m},Y_{in}(Z_i):i\in S_m)\).

symbols.name: delta
symbols.def: Arbitrary pilot-measurable normalized centered score rule.

symbols.name: Ghat
symbols.def: Nuisance-efficient empirical plug-in score rule formed from an efficient estimator of \(\beta\).

symbols.name: tauhat
symbols.def: \(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}_{n,m}(\delta_m)=(m/n)\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_{S_m}(0)+(N/n)\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\delta_m)\).

symbols.name: Rn
symbols.def: \(R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)=E_{\beta}E[(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}_{n,m}(\delta_m)-\boldsymbol\tau_n)^{\mathsf T}W(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}_{n,m}(\delta_m)-\boldsymbol\tau_n)\mid\mathbf X_n]\).

symbols.name: Ror
symbols.def: \(R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)=V_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(G_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta),\beta)\), the matching experiment-indexed full-array empirical raw-MSE oracle risk.

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: Oracle opportunity-cost coefficient \(A(\beta)\), derived by \(\mathrm{thm{:}oracle\text{-}deletion\text{-}loss}\).

symbols.name: Gamma
symbols.def: \(\Gamma_{ab}(\beta)=\frac{1-\eta}{2\alpha}f_{\beta}(q_{\alpha,\beta})\mathcal C_{ab}(\beta,q_{\alpha,\beta})\) for \(a,b\le r\), the Gaussian acceptance-boundary Hessian induced by the common experiment-indexed oracle limit and the continuous coarea conditional-covariance version.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: \(B(\beta)=\operatorname{tr}\{\Gamma(\beta)I_{\mathrm{eff}}(\beta)^{-1}\}\), with \(\Gamma\) defined from the continuous coarea boundary covariance of the common experiment-indexed limit \(G_{\infty}\).

symbols.name: En
symbols.def: For \(m\in\mathcal M_n\), \(\mathcal E_n(m)=\inf_{\delta_m}\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}[R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)]_{+}\).

symbols.name: Phi
symbols.def: \(\Phi(t)=\max_{\beta\in\mathcal K}\{A(\beta)t+B(\beta)/t\}\).

symbols.name: tstar
symbols.def: \(t^{\star}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{t>0}\Phi(t)\).

symbols.name: Cstar
symbols.def: \(C^{\star}=\Phi(t^{\star})\).

symbols.name: Model
symbols.def: Class \(\mathfrak M\) of deterministic-baseline triangular arrays and conditional outcome families used below.

symbols.name: HDModel
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{HD}}\), the deterministic finite-population array class in Han and Deng's Assumptions 3 and 4, excluding their allocation-share restriction.

symbols.name: RealizedModel
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak R_{\beta}(\mathfrak M)\), the probability-one realization class of deterministic baseline and potential-outcome arrays generated by \(P_{\beta}\).

novel.justification: Manufacturing and laboratory replications can preregister the complete future batch covariates before treatment, so all parameter information arrives through randomized outcomes.

standard.name: Bounded sufficient form of the finite-population Lindeberg condition

novel.justification: Independent bounded conditional responses with common coefficients across consecutive production batches form a concrete stable family for replicated factorial process experiments.

assumptions.condition: \((x,\beta)\mapsto\int y^a p_{q,\beta}(dy\mid x)\in C^3(\operatorname{supp}\nu\times\mathcal U)\quad(a=1,2,\ q\in\mathcal Q)\).

novel.justification: Bounded logistic, beta-regression, and smooth location families on compact preregistered baseline domains have continuously varying first two outcome moments.
Bounded generalized-linear conditional outcome families with freely varying regression coefficients and dispersion coordinates contain such connected product neighborhoods inside a regular chart.

standard.name: Uniform local asymptotic normality moment condition

assumptions.condition: \(D_{\lambda}G_T(\beta)=0\) for every \(n\), every balanced \(T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and every \(\beta\in\mathcal K\).

novel.justification: Conditional outcome models can separate covariate-slope directions determining balance geometry from intercept and dispersion directions that affect likelihood but not the oracle score.
Smooth bounded regression families away from score-rank changes induce three-times differentiable effect-specific covariance and oracle-score maps.

assumptions.condition: \(\operatorname{rank}\{G_T(\beta)\}=\operatorname{rank}\{G_{\infty}(\beta)\}=r_G\) for every \(n\), every balanced \(T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and every \(\beta\in\mathcal K\).

novel.justification: Experiments with stable nonzero outcome--covariate associations and no eigenvalue crossings lie in a constant-rank stratum of quadratic balance geometries.
Distinct, nondegenerate effect-specific balance priorities give positive curvature after quotienting scale and score stabilizers; smooth disk regression families provide an explicit example.

definitions.name: Normalized centered ellipsoidal actions
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal H_T=\{H:\ H=0\ \text{or}\ H\in\mathbb S_{+}^{Fp},\ \operatorname{tr}(H)=1;\ a_{T,H}\text{ is the centered lower-tail rule on }\Omega_T\}\).

definitions.name: Empirical-oracle boundary handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{fin}}\): couple the exact score ordering on \(\Omega_T\) to the Gaussian quadratic ordering at the realized \(G_T(\beta)\); control thin-boundary probabilities and score-weighted truncated moments jointly; then insert exact first- and second-order inclusion probabilities into the Horvitz--Thompson covariance identity.

definitions.name: Nuisance-efficient local action handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{eff}}\): estimate \(\beta\) in the pilot by an efficient score after projection on the nuisance tangent space, map the oracle coordinate into \(G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta)\), and apply the exact mixture construction on the main wave.

statements.statement: For every \(\beta\in\mathcal K\), \[\mathfrak R_{\beta}(\mathfrak M)\subsetneq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{HD}}.\]
statements.justification: The inclusion records exactly how the new likelihood-rich planning domain relates to the closest published finite-population class.
statements.gap: Han and Deng's population framework supports first-order randomization limits but has no outcome-likelihood chart on which nuisance-efficient local pilot regret is defined.
statements.consumer: It prevents the square-root achievability result from being misreported as uniform over every array allowed by Han and Deng.

statements.statement: For every \((\mathbf X_n,P_{\beta,n})\in\mathfrak M\), every realized bounded potential-outcome table and every pilot-measurable \(\delta_m\), \(E[\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}_{n,m}(\delta_m)\mid\mathbf Y_n,\mathbf X_n]=\boldsymbol\tau_n\) and \[R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)=d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)-(N/n)^2E_{S_m}d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta)+(N/n)^2E\{V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\delta_m,\beta)-V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta),\beta)\}.\] This identity remains exact under randomized ties and unequal \(\pi_{iq}\), a case not represented by the ordinary symmetric factorial estimator of Branson, Dasgupta, and Rubin.
statements.justification: Exact centering isolates pilot opportunity cost from learned-action regret without symmetry assumptions.
statements.gap: Horvitz and Thompson give fixed-design unbiasedness, while Branson, Dasgupta, and Rubin use symmetric factorial rerandomization; neither supplies this pilot-conditional pooled identity under a learned unequal-inclusion law.
statements.consumer: It permits unbiased reuse of both waves in sequential factorial cycles whose learned acceptance rule is not label symmetric.

statements.statement: For every \(T\) and \(\beta\in\mathcal K\), the construction \(G_T(\beta)\) belongs to \(\mathcal H_T\), and \(p_{T,G_T(\beta)}\) has exact acceptance mass \(\alpha\) and support bounded below by \(\eta/|\Omega_T|\).
statements.justification: The oracle comparator must itself be a legal positive-support exact-alpha design on every finite assignment support.
statements.gap: The published raw oracle is an asymptotic quadratic criterion; legality under the present exact boundary randomization is an auxiliary finite-design obligation.
statements.consumer: It ensures that every reported oracle contrast compares two implementable assignment distributions.

statements.statement: The score \(\widehat G_m\) constructed by \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{eff}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal H_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}\) almost surely, and its induced main-wave design has exact acceptance mass \(\alpha\) and support bounded below by \(\eta/|\Omega_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}|\).
statements.justification: Efficient score estimation must not compromise finite randomization validity or positive inclusion probabilities.
statements.gap: Pilot plug-in rerandomization is first-order valid in Han and Deng, but the exact-alpha positive-support normalization here is a distinct finite construction.
statements.consumer: It makes the learned rule auditable before any asymptotic risk comparison is invoked.

statements.justification: Positive assignment support makes every permitted one-wave Horvitz--Thompson risk uniformly first order even on irregular subsets.
statements.gap: General Horvitz--Thompson consistency does not provide a constant uniform over the present pilot-indexed rerandomization actions.
statements.consumer: It rules out apparent gains from assigning only a vanishing main wave and controls rare singular pilot complements.

statements.statement: For every member of \(\mathfrak M\) there is a common \(G_{\infty}\in C^3(\mathcal K;\mathbb S_{+}^{Fp})\) such that, for every balanced \(m=m(n)\) with \(m\to\infty\), \(N\to\infty\), and \(m/n\to0\), \[\max_{0\le j\le3}\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}\lVert D_{\rho}^{j}G_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)-D_{\rho}^{j}G_{\infty}(\beta)\rVert\to0,\] and \[\max_{0\le j\le3}\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}\lVert D_{\rho}^{j}G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta)-D_{\rho}^{j}G_{\infty}(\beta)\rVert\xrightarrow{P_{S_m}}0.\] Here \(D_{\rho}^{0}G=G\), the first display is deterministic conditional on the complete baseline array, and the second probability is over the uniform pilot split conditional on that array.
statements.justification: The common experiment-indexed limit removes ambiguity about which empirical oracle and which convergence mode define the boundary constants.
statements.gap: First-order learned-rerandomization arguments require consistency of one selected score, whereas the second-order boundary expansion needs uniform convergence of the oracle map and its first three quotient derivatives along both realized experiment sequences.
statements.consumer: It gives replication planners one stable limiting geometry whether the oracle is evaluated on all registered units or on the random main-wave complement.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(\beta\in\mathcal K\) and balanced sequences with \(m\to\infty\), \(N\to\infty\), and \(m/n\to0\), \[d_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)-(N/n)^2E_{S_m}d_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta)=A(\beta)\frac{m}{n^2}+o\!\left(\frac{m}{n^2}+\frac{1}{nm}\right),\] where \(A\) is continuous and \(0<\inf_{\beta\in\mathcal K}A(\beta)\le\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}A(\beta)<\infty\).
statements.justification: This term prices the irreversible loss from assigning pilot units before the oracle geometry is learned.
statements.gap: Han and Deng establish first-order equivalence after sample splitting but do not retain the deletion contrast at order \(m/n^2\).
statements.consumer: It lets a replication planner quantify the marginal precision price of adding pilot batches.

statements.statement: For the common limit \(G_{\infty}\), the map \(\beta\mapsto q_{\alpha,\beta}\) is continuous, \(0<q_{\alpha,\beta}<\infty\), and \[0<\inf_{\beta\in\mathcal K}f_{\beta}(q_{\alpha,\beta})\le\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}f_{\beta}(q_{\alpha,\beta})<\infty.\] The coarea version \(\mathcal C(\beta,u)\) is continuous on a neighborhood of \(\{(\beta,q_{\alpha,\beta}):\beta\in\mathcal K\}\); consequently \(\Gamma(\beta)\) and \(B(\beta)=\operatorname{tr}\{\Gamma(\beta)I_{\mathrm{eff}}(\beta)^{-1}\}\) are continuous on \(\mathcal K\).
statements.justification: Uniform coarea control makes the moving Gaussian acceptance boundary differentiable without adding a separate density assumption.
statements.gap: Existing rerandomization limits use fixed quadratic forms; the uniform statement over an empirical-oracle chart is an auxiliary bridge to second order.
statements.consumer: It supplies the stable quantile derivative needed to translate efficient pilot uncertainty into action regret.

statements.statement: For every balanced sequence \(m=m(n)\) with \(m\to\infty\), \(N\to\infty\), and \(m/n\to0\), and every interior \(\beta_0\in\mathcal K^{\circ}\), \[\lim_{c\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\delta_m}\sup_{\substack{\beta=\beta_0+(h,u)/\sqrt m\in\mathcal K,\ h\in\mathbb R^r,\ u\in\mathbb R^s\\\lVert(h,u)\rVert\le c}}nm\,(N/n)^2E\{V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\delta_m,\beta)-V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta),\beta)\}=B(\beta_0).\] The infimum ranges over all pilot-measurable normalized centered score rules. The rule \(\widehat G_m\) satisfies \[\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}\left|nm\,(N/n)^2E\{V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\widehat G_m,\beta)-V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta),\beta)\}-B(\beta)\right|\to0,\] where expectations include the random complement and pilot outcomes, and \(B(\beta)=\operatorname{tr}\{\Gamma(\beta)I_{\mathrm{eff}}(\beta)^{-1}\}\) uses the continuous coarea boundary covariance of \(G_{\infty}\).
statements.justification: The trace constant converts nuisance-efficient pilot information into the unavoidable quadratic loss from selecting a rerandomization geometry.
statements.gap: Liu, Han, Rubin, and Deng integrate over prior uncertainty, and Armstrong gives first-order superpopulation efficiency bounds; neither derives this finite-population exact-alpha local design game.
statements.consumer: It identifies which pilot outcomes and nuisance directions determine the precision value of another learning batch.

statements.statement: Can the handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{fin}}\) establish, uniformly over \(\mathfrak M\), exact ties, arbitrary balanced deterministic baseline lattices, local action displacements of order \(m^{-1/2}\), and unequal inclusion probabilities, that the finite Horvitz--Thompson action regret on \(T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}\) differs from the continuous-coarea Gaussian boundary quadratic form of \(G_{\infty}\) by \(o(m^{-1})\) in probability over the split, and that the contrast between \(T_n^{\mathrm{full}}\) and \(T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}\) has no additional lattice or inclusion correction at order \(m/n^2+1/(nm)\)?
statements.justification: This is the proof boundary on which the advertised second-order constant is valid or must acquire a finite-randomization correction.
statements.gap: Li and Ding provide a first-order random-partition central limit theorem, and Wang and Li provide quantitative Gaussian control for best-choice rerandomization; neither controls score-weighted moving-boundary moments at this scale.
statements.consumer: A positive answer validates smooth pilot rules on integer-valued manufacturing baselines; a negative answer identifies the correction planners must include.

statements.statement: For the nuisance-efficient exact-alpha rule \(\widehat G_m\) and every balanced sequence \(m=m(n)\) with \(m\to\infty\), \(N\to\infty\), and \(m/n\to0\), \[\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}\frac{\left|R_{n,m}(\widehat G_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)-A(\beta)m/n^2-B(\beta)/(nm)\right|}{m/n^2+1/(nm)}\to0.\] Here \(R_n^{\mathrm{or}}\) uses \(T_n^{\mathrm{full}}\), the learned action is evaluated on \(T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}\), and \(B\) is induced by the common limit \(G_{\infty}\) and its continuous coarea boundary covariance. Moreover, the first term and the local minimax second term are jointly sharp among all pilot-measurable actions. This gives a second-order oracle-precision comparison on the explicitly narrower likelihood-rich subclass of Han and Deng's finite-population setting.
statements.justification: The expansion exposes the two forces that determine pilot size below first order and supplies their sharp coefficients.
statements.gap: Han and Deng prove consistency and first-order oracle precision but explicitly leave optimal learning-sample choice to refined asymptotics; no checked closer paper supplies these two coefficients.
statements.consumer: It converts an informal learning fraction into a sample-size-dependent rule for repeated factorial production experiments.

statements.statement: For every admissible balanced pilot-size sequence \(m=m(n)\in\mathcal M_n\) with \(m/\sqrt n\to0\) or \(m/\sqrt n\to\infty\), including bounded \(m\), positive pilot fractions, and \(N=o(n)\), \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m)=\infty.\]
statements.justification: Endpoint exclusion is needed to promote the interior expansion from a candidate scale to the unique global pilot scale.
statements.gap: First-order oracle equivalence does not compare bounded, vanishing, macroscopic, and nearly all-pilot sequences on one risk scale.
statements.consumer: It prevents a planner from exploiting a degenerate pilot or main wave that appears favorable only because the interior approximation was used outside its domain.

statements.statement: The quantity \(\inf_{\ell\in\mathcal M_n}\mathcal E_n(\ell)\) is positive for all sufficiently large \(n\). Let \(m=m(n)\in\mathcal M_n\) satisfy the explicit asymptotic-minimax condition \[\frac{\mathcal E_n(m)}{\inf_{\ell\in\mathcal M_n}\mathcal E_n(\ell)}\to1.\] Then \[\frac{m}{\sqrt n}\to t^{\star},\qquad n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m)\to C^{\star}=\min_{t>0}\max_{\beta\in\mathcal K}\{A(\beta)t+B(\beta)/t\}.\] Here \(A\) is the full-array versus random-complement deletion coefficient and \(B\) is the continuous-coarea curvature coefficient induced by the common limit \(G_{\infty}\). The minimizer \(t^{\star}\) is unique, and \[C^{\star}=\max_{(a,b)\in\operatorname{conv}\{(A(\beta),B(\beta)):\beta\in\mathcal K\}}2\sqrt{ab}.\] An optimizer of the last display has a certificate supported on at most two parameter values active at \(t^{\star}\).
statements.justification: The theorem turns the pointwise expansion into a unique globally defensible pilot rule with a finite certificate.
statements.gap: Yamin's binary-arm global boundary analysis gives an approximately optimal \(n^{2/3}\) plan, whereas this locally rich factorial geometry requires a sharp square-root constant and a different empirical oracle.
statements.consumer: Stable-batch replications of Menon, Chakrabarti, and Nerella's sequential factorial workflow can preregister the learning-wave size from a two-state worst-case certificate.

statements.statement: If \(p_{T,H}\) is invariant under the treatment-label flip group, then \(\pi_{iq}(T,H)=1/Q\) for all \(i\in T\) and \(q\in\mathcal Q\), so \(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(H)\) equals the ordinary balanced factorial difference-in-means estimator. With fixed \(H\), its first-order limit reduces to the symmetric truncated-Gaussian factorial law of Li, Ding, and Rubin; with \(H=0\) in both waves, the pooled assignment has the full-sample balanced complete-randomization marginal.
statements.justification: The reduction checks that exact-inclusion analysis preserves the established symmetric factorial design as a special case.
statements.gap: The proposition is a required compatibility result rather than a novelty claim; the new content begins when pilot adaptation breaks label symmetry.
statements.consumer: Practitioners can use the standard estimator whenever their preregistered score retains the flip symmetry.

sampling_model.design: A uniform balanced pilot split, balanced complete randomization on \(S_m\), and a pilot-measurable positive-support exact-alpha ellipsoidal mixture on \(T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}=S_m^c\), compared with the full-array oracle on \(T_n^{\mathrm{full}}\).
sampling_model.units: A deterministic triangular array of \(n\) units with complete bounded baselines known before assignment and fixed realized potential outcomes for design-based inference.
sampling_model.treatment: All \(Q=2^{K_f}\) combinations receive equal wave-specific counts.
sampling_model.overlap: The fixed mixture weight \(\eta>0\) gives every balanced assignment positive probability and every unit--combination inclusion positive probability.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Pilot outcomes identify \(\beta=(\rho,\lambda)\); the oracle coordinate is estimated after efficient projection on the nuisance score, the baseline array contributes no likelihood information, and the random-complement oracle map converges with three quotient derivatives in probability over the pilot split to the same \(G_{\infty}\) as the full-array map.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The learned factorial rerandomization procedure achieves the same first-order asymptotic precision as its oracle under suitable conditions.
The pooled binary-arm conditional-minimax-regret plan uses an \(n^{2/3}\) pilot and is approximately worst-case optimal.
The two-stage Bayesian rerandomization procedure learns covariate importance from a pilot and improves first-order precision.
Inverse inclusion weighting gives unbiased estimation under unequal-probability sampling without replacement.
The Horvitz--Thompson estimator is quadratically mean consistent under broad general designs.
Finite-population random partitions obey joint central limit theorems for multiple treatments and vector outcomes.
Fixed symmetric factorial rerandomization yields a truncated-Gaussian joint limit and conservative confidence regions.
Finite-population Gaussian approximation supports large-sample inference for best-choice Mahalanobis rerandomization.
Symmetric rerandomization preserves unbiasedness of ordinary factorial-effect estimators.
Quadratic-form rerandomization criteria admit fixed-geometry precision comparisons and a minimax Euclidean choice.
Sequential superpopulation experiments have first-order semiparametric efficiency bounds under adaptive assignment.

tldr: A balanced pilot learns which covariate imbalances matter for a vector of factorial effects, and an exact-alpha positive-support ellipsoidal mixture uses that information in the main wave. The full-array oracle map and the random-complement oracle map, the latter in probability over the pilot split, converge uniformly with three quotient derivatives to one \(G_{\infty}\); its continuous coarea boundary covariance defines \(B(\beta)=\operatorname{tr}\{\Gamma(\beta)I_{\mathrm{eff}}(\beta)^{-1}\}\). Relative to the matching full-array empirical oracle, the exact-inclusion pooled Horvitz--Thompson estimator has the sharp uniform contrast \(A(\beta)m/n^2+B(\beta)/(nm)\). Any pilot sequence whose minimax excess-risk ratio to the best admissible balanced size tends to one has the unique scale \(m/\sqrt n\to t^{\star}\), with a global constant certified by at most two active parameter values. The open mathematical core is a lattice- and tie-uniform finite-randomization comparison that validates these coefficients for unequal exact inclusions and arbitrary pilot-measurable actions.

project_justification.gap: The closest factorial procedure reaches its oracle only at first order and explicitly leaves the learning-sample proportion open. Binary-arm pilot theory gives a different global boundary rate, while general Horvitz--Thompson and rerandomization theory stop at exact unbiasedness, consistency, or first-order Gaussian limits.
project_justification.niche: A fixed complete baseline array and a connected full-dimensional conditional-outcome chart isolate a locally regular design problem in which pilot opportunity cost and oracle-action curvature coexist at the \(n^{-3/2}\) scale.
project_justification.fill: The project derives a common experiment-indexed oracle limit with uniform derivative convergence, defines its boundary curvature by continuous coarea disintegration, obtains both risk coefficients, proves the local arbitrary-action lower bound and efficient upper bound, controls exact ties and unequal inclusions, and converts the expansion into a unique global pilot constant through an explicit asymptotic-minimax risk ratio.

related_work: Han and Deng's Theorem 8 supplies the closest factorial-vector sample-splitting architecture and first-order oracle equivalence; the present theorem targets the smaller risk terms that their Section 6 leaves unresolved within the explicitly narrower likelihood-rich subclass recorded in Proposition 1. Yamin's Appendix E supplies the pooled opportunity-cost versus action-regret accounting, but its binary Neyman-allocation boundary class yields an \(n^{2/3}\) plan and informs rather than determines the local factorial result. Liu, Han, Rubin, and Deng optimize prior-integrated asymptotic variance and motivate covariance-aware rerandomization, but do not give a frequentist nuisance-efficient local minimax boundary. Horvitz and Thompson provide the exact inverse-inclusion identity, and Delevoye and Sävje provide broad consistency; neither gives a pilot-conditional second-order factorial risk expansion. Li and Ding's random-partition theorem and Li, Ding, and Rubin's truncated-Gaussian factorial law are the first-order finite-population foundations. Wang and Li quantify Gaussian approximation under selective rerandomization, but their result does not control a moving exact-alpha boundary at the proposed risk scale. Branson, Dasgupta, and Rubin establish the symmetric factorial benchmark to which the exact-inclusion estimator reduces. Menon, Chakrabarti, and Nerella document the practical sequence of factorial product-development cycles; the present consumer claim is prospective and additionally requires preregistered future baselines and a stable rich response family.
technical_internal_limitation: An exact four-unit nonsymmetric score example has positive support, acceptance probability \(137/1000\), inclusion probabilities \(1/16\) and \(7/16\), and zero Horvitz--Thompson bias, yet its empirical-oracle exact risk is discontinuous as a score coordinate crosses zero. Thus smooth outcome likelihoods do not justify continuity of finite score orderings. The theorem must use worst-case suprema and prove that any lattice discontinuity is below \(m/n^2+1/(nm)\); it may not assume finite-risk continuity or finite maximum attainment.
honest_scope: Exact Horvitz--Thompson centering, the \(O(|T|^{-1})\) one-wave risk bound under positive support, the continuous-coarea Gaussian boundary Hessian calculation, and the deterministic convex-envelope certificate have verified proof routes in the presolve evidence but remain marked to prove in this proposal core. Uniform convergence of \(G_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}\) and its first three quotient derivatives is deterministic conditional on the complete baseline array; the corresponding convergence for \(G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}\) is in probability over the uniform pilot split. The central uniform finite-randomization expansion, exact-inclusion perturbation bound, arbitrary-action localization, and nuisance-efficient local minimax transfer are open. The probability-one realized population class is a strict subclass of Han and Deng's published finite-population class because efficient pilot information is not defined on their unparameterized arrays; the achievability claim is not asserted beyond this subclass. Rank crossings, weak oracle signals, informative random baselines, finite parameter catalogues, and shifted noncentered actions are excluded. Under treatment-label symmetry, the estimator and first-order law reduce to the established ordinary factorial rerandomization result.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Sections 3.3 and 4.1--4.5, Theorem 8 and Section 6 of arXiv:2609.02078v1.
seed_details.kernel: Derive the uniform empirical-oracle risk expansion \(A(\beta)m/n^{2}+B(\beta)/(nm)+o(m/n^{2}+1/(nm))\), then characterize the globally minimax pilot constant and its two-active-state certificate.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Han and Deng prove consistency of the learned importance matrix and first-order oracle precision, but their discussion explicitly leaves the optimal learning-sample proportion open.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Retain the deletion loss from withholding \(m\) units and the local decision loss from estimating the oracle score, instead of applying Slutsky after consistency of the score estimate.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for factorial rerandomization combined with pilot size, empirical oracle, second-order risk, exact inclusion, and curvature found no theorem with this expansion.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Han and Deng because their learned score already has oracle asymptotic precision.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their result discards both terms at the \(n^{-3/2}\) scale and does not optimize a vanishing pilot against the matching full-sample empirical oracle.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Sections 3.2--4, Theorem 6, Section 7 and Supplement B.4 of arXiv:2303.07904.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize a nuisance-efficient locally minimax randomized ellipsoidal action with exact acceptance probability and positive assignment support near competing oracle geometries.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The Bayesian criterion integrates variance under a prior and its two-stage implementation uses fixed pilot fractions; it does not identify the frequentist Gaussian boundary experiment or the efficient regret trace.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the fixed prior second moment by the pilot's efficient local Gaussian experiment and solve the constrained randomized-action problem at oracle boundaries.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing local asymptotic minimaxity, exact-alpha rerandomization, positive support, factorial effects, and efficient information found no direct result.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Bayesian rerandomization by taking its prior to be the pilot posterior.
seed_details.rebuttal: A posterior plug-in does not yield the frequentist local minimax lower bound, the nuisance-efficient covariance, or exact finite assignment support.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Publisher abstract and the defining unbiased total and joint-inclusion variance construction in the original unequal-probability framework.
seed_details.kernel: Obtain exact conditional unbiasedness and a uniform second-order raw-MSE expansion for a pooled factorial Horvitz--Thompson vector under a pilot-generated unequal-probability assignment law.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Classical identities give exact first moments and variances for a fixed design, not a random pilot-indexed design whose inclusion probabilities change through exact ties.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Condition on the pilot, calculate first- and second-order treatment-combination inclusions, and retain their deviations in the factorial covariance identity before averaging over the random split.
seed_details.destination_search: The closest general result is Delevoye and Sävje's quadratic-mean consistency; no pilot-conditional factorial expansion at order \(1/(nm)\) was located.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from the Horvitz--Thompson variance identity by conditioning on the pilot.
seed_details.rebuttal: The identity is algebraic; the uniform expansion requires new control of random exact inclusions and boundary mass at a smaller order than ordinary consistency.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, main Gaussian-approximation results and discussion of arXiv:2312.02513; the paper studies quantitative first-order approximation under selective rerandomization.
seed_details.kernel: Prove a conditional local-limit expansion for quadratic risk through an exact-alpha ellipsoidal boundary, uniformly over deterministic lattice baseline arrays and randomized ties.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Berry--Esseen control for an unconditional imbalance vector does not automatically control a risk expectation after conditioning on a moving, pilot-estimated boundary.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the global convex-set probability bound by a thin-boundary probability-and-truncated-moment comparison centered at the realized empirical oracle.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for Edgeworth or local-limit expansions combined with exact rerandomization ties and factorial Horvitz--Thompson risk found no occupied target.
seed_details.red_team: A standard Berry--Esseen theorem makes lattice and tie errors negligible.
seed_details.rebuttal: The available error is too large at the \(n^{-3/2}\) risk scale unless boundary displacement and loss are coupled; exact ties can change inclusions discontinuously.
seed_details.disposition: dropped as a standalone seed after deepening because its entire value is the finite-comparison lemma inside S1

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Sections 2.3--2.4 and Appendices E.2--E.5 of arXiv:2607.16982v2.
seed_details.kernel: Derive a critical curvature sequence separating the locally regular \(m\asymp n^{1/2}\) regime from the global boundary \(m\asymp n^{2/3}\) regime.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Yamin's worst-case variance-allocation game yields the two-thirds scale, while locally quadratic ellipsoidal action regret suggests a square-root scale; no common curvature frontier is supplied.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Localize the oracle action loss with a possibly vanishing Hessian and balance its induced pilot regret against empirical-oracle opportunity cost.
seed_details.destination_search: Joint searches for pilot-size phase transition, action curvature, rerandomization, and two-wave regret did not reveal a derived critical sequence.
seed_details.red_team: This is only a relabeling of regular versus nonregular decision theory.
seed_details.rebuttal: A defensible version requires a design-computable curvature frontier and matching upper and lower pilot scales, which neither anchor derives.
seed_details.disposition: dropped after deepening because the required common class and observable frontier were not supported by the available exact factorial analysis

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Sections 3.2--3.3 and 7 of arXiv:2303.07904, including the prior-integrated variance criterion and its scale invariance.
seed_details.kernel: Establish equivalence of Bayesian-mixture and plug-in-oracle ellipsoids away from score boundaries and derive the local sequence on which their risks diverge.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The Bayesian criterion and plug-in criterion are compared numerically and by first-order efficiency, not through a local divergence threshold for factorial-vector loss.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Expand both acceptance measures around a common oracle boundary and identify the covariance-to-curvature ratio controlling their risk difference.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing Bayesian rerandomization, plug-in oracle, equivalence frontier, and factorial effects found only first-order or simulation comparisons.
seed_details.red_team: The two designs differ only by replacing a point estimate with its posterior second moment.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Section 4.5, Theorem 8, Section 4.6 and the proof architecture in Appendix A.12--A.16 of arXiv:2609.02078v1.

seed_details.proof_boundary: Han and Deng's joint limit is stated under learning-sample conditions used for first-order consistency and an ordinary weighted estimator, not exact unequal inclusions at a vanishing share.

seed_details.red_team: Coverage follows immediately from the existing joint central limit theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The existing limit does not cover the exact unequal-inclusion estimator or the second-order pilot-optimal triangular array, but the contribution is secondary to the risk frontier.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Abstract, introduction and the quadratic-form optimality comparisons in arXiv:2403.12815.
seed_details.kernel: Choose a positive-support pilot-adaptive mixture that is minimax over local rank crossings of the oracle quadratic form and certify its regret.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Quadratic-form comparisons treat a fixed geometry; score eigenvalue collisions make the oracle quotient chart and its curvature singular.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace smooth fixed-rank score coordinates by a stratified tangent cone and solve the resulting nonsmooth Gaussian design game.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for rank-crossing adaptive rerandomization and tangent-cone minimax design found no direct treatment.
seed_details.red_team: Scale normalization and eigenvalue ordering remove the singularity.
seed_details.rebuttal: They remove representational duplication but not a genuine change in rank or stabilizer dimension; nevertheless this lies outside the regular chart required for a feasible first paper.

novelty_justification: The selected kernel moves beyond Han and Deng's first-order oracle equivalence in the direction their Section 6 leaves open: it identifies the vanishing learning-sample order and its constant on an explicitly narrower full-dimensional fixed-baseline outcome chart where efficient pilot information is defined. It differs from Yamin's global binary-arm variance-allocation problem because the locally quadratic factorial ellipsoid loss yields \(1/m\) action regret and a square-root pilot, while exact-inclusion Horvitz--Thompson risk and empirical-oracle deletion loss are retained. The closest unequal-probability and rerandomization papers supply first-moment identities or first-order limits, not a uniform conditional expansion through random exact-alpha boundaries. The load-bearing novelty is therefore the finite-randomization comparison, not Gaussian oracle geometry, ordinary local asymptotic normality, or the deterministic envelope alone.
